source: Figures from the d3-celestial line set, copyright Olaf Frohn, BSD 3-Clause licence; stars from the Yale Bright Star Catalogue; facts from Wikipedia.

constellations.name: Andromeda
constellations.story: In Greek myth, Andromeda was the princess chained to a rock as an offering to the sea monster Cetus, then saved by Perseus.

constellations.name: Antlia
constellations.story: Lacaille established it in the 18th century as Antlia Pneumatica, the air pump, one of his constellations depicting scientific instruments.

constellations.name: Apus
constellations.story: Its Greek name means without feet, because Europeans once wrongly believed that birds-of-paradise had no feet.

constellations.name: Aquarius
constellations.story: One of the oldest constellations of the zodiac, the water-carrier is sometimes identified in Greek myth with Ganymede, cupbearer to the gods.

constellations.name: Aquila
constellations.story: Often said in Greek myth to be the eagle that carried Zeus's thunderbolts; its brightest star, Altair, is a corner of the Summer Triangle.

constellations.name: Ara
constellations.story: In Greek myth it was the altar where the gods made offerings and formed an alliance before defeating the Titans.

constellations.name: Aries
constellations.story: Associated in Greek myth with the golden ram that rescued Phrixus and Helle and carried Phrixus to Colchis.

constellations.name: Auriga
constellations.story: The charioteer is often identified in Greek myth with Erichthonius of Athens, credited with inventing the four-horse chariot.

constellations.name: Boötes
constellations.story: The herdsman or ploughman holds Arcturus, the brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere and fourth-brightest in the night sky.

constellations.name: Caelum
constellations.story: Lacaille introduced the engraver's chisel in the 1750s; it is the eighth-smallest constellation, and its brightest star is only magnitude 4.45.

constellations.name: Camelopardalis
constellations.story: A large but faint constellation of the far northern sky representing a giraffe, introduced by Petrus Plancius in 1612 or 1613.

constellations.name: Cancer
constellations.story: In Greek myth, the crab that bit Heracles as he fought the Hydra, placed among the stars by Hera; it holds the Beehive Cluster.

constellations.name: Canes Venatici
constellations.story: Created by Johannes Hevelius in the 17th century, it is usually drawn as the hunting dogs of Boötes the herdsman.

constellations.name: Canis Major
constellations.story: Usually drawn following Orion the hunter, the greater dog contains Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, known as the Dog Star.

constellations.name: Canis Minor
constellations.story: The lesser dog that follows Orion; Ptolemy listed it as a pattern of just two stars, Procyon and Gomeisa.

constellations.name: Capricornus
constellations.story: Usually drawn as a sea goat, half goat and half fish, it is the smallest constellation of the zodiac.

constellations.name: Carina
constellations.story: The keel of the great ship Argo Navis, which Lacaille divided into three; it holds Canopus, the second-brightest star in the night sky.

constellations.name: Cassiopeia
constellations.story: In Greek myth, Cassiopeia was the vain queen who boasted of her beauty, mother of Andromeda; five bright stars form its distinctive W.

constellations.name: Centaurus
constellations.story: Ovid says it honours the wise centaur Chiron, tutor of heroes; it contains Alpha Centauri, the nearest star system to the Sun.

constellations.name: Cepheus
constellations.story: Named after a king of Aethiopia in Greek myth, father of Andromeda; its star Delta Cephei is the prototype of the Cepheid variables.

constellations.name: Cetus
constellations.story: In Greek myth Cetus was the sea monster to which Andromeda was offered; its star Mira was the first variable star to be discovered.

constellations.name: Chamaeleon
constellations.story: One of twelve constellations created by Petrus Plancius from the observations of the Dutch navigators Keyser and de Houtman in the 1590s.

constellations.name: Circinus
constellations.story: Lacaille introduced it in 1756 to represent the drafting compass used for drawing circles, not the mariner's compass of Pyxis.

constellations.name: Columba
constellations.story: Plancius first drew it in 1592 and named it Noah's Dove, the bird that told Noah the Great Flood was receding.

constellations.name: Coma Berenices
constellations.story: Berenice's Hair honours Queen Berenice II of Egypt, who sacrificed her long hair; it is the only constellation named after a historical person.

constellations.name: Corona Australis
constellations.story: The ancient Greeks saw this southern crown as a wreath rather than a crown, and associated it with Sagittarius or Centaurus.

constellations.name: Corona Borealis
constellations.story: In classical myth it usually represents the crown that Dionysus gave to the Cretan princess Ariadne, who set it in the heavens.

constellations.name: Corvus
constellations.story: A raven linked with stories of the god Apollo, drawn perched on the back of Hydra the water snake.

constellations.name: Crater
constellations.story: Named after the Greek krater, a cup for watering down wine, it is linked with Apollo and sits on the back of Hydra.

constellations.name: Crux
constellations.story: The smallest of the 88 constellations; its brightest stars appear on the national flags of New Zealand, Australia, Brazil, Papua New Guinea and Samoa.

constellations.name: Cygnus
constellations.story: Greek myth links the swan with several legends, including Zeus in disguise; its brightest stars form the Northern Cross.

constellations.name: Delphinus
constellations.story: Its brightest stars, Sualocin and Rotanev, spell Nicolaus Venator backwards, the Latinised name of a Palermo Observatory director.

constellations.name: Dorado
constellations.story: Named after the mahi-mahi, called dorado in Spanish, it contains most of the Large Magellanic Cloud and the south ecliptic pole.

constellations.name: Draco
constellations.story: The north ecliptic pole lies in the dragon; Eratosthenes identified it with Ladon, guardian of the golden apples of the Hesperides.

constellations.name: Equuleus
constellations.story: The little horse is the second-smallest of the 88 constellations, after Crux, and has no star brighter than fourth magnitude.

constellations.name: Eridanus
constellations.story: A celestial river linked in Greek myth with Phaethon, who lost control of the Sun's chariot; it is the sixth-largest constellation.

constellations.name: Fornax
constellations.story: Lacaille named it in the 1750s after a chemical furnace; it contains the patch of sky photographed by Hubble as the Ultra-Deep Field.

constellations.name: Gemini
constellations.story: Named for the twins Castor and Pollux of Greek myth, whose names are carried by its two brightest stars.

constellations.name: Grus
constellations.story: Petrus Plancius created the crane in the 1590s, partly from stars once counted as the tail of Piscis Austrinus, the Southern Fish.

constellations.name: Hercules
constellations.story: Named after the Greek hero Heracles, it is the fifth-largest constellation and the largest with no star brighter than magnitude 2.5.

constellations.name: Horologium
constellations.story: Lacaille pictured these faint stars in 1756 as a pendulum clock; Alpha Horologii is its only star brighter than magnitude 4.

constellations.name: Hydra
constellations.story: The largest of the 88 constellations; Greek myth links it with a water snake Apollo cast into the sky, or the many-headed Hydra.

constellations.name: Hydrus
constellations.story: Plancius created this male water snake in the 1590s as a small counterpart to Hydra; Beta Hydri lies close to the south celestial pole.

constellations.name: Indus
constellations.story: Plancius mapped it by 1598; its name means the Indian, apparently representing an inhabitant of Madagascar or the East Indies.

constellations.name: Lacerta
constellations.story: Hevelius defined the lizard in 1687; its brightest stars form a W shape, earning it the nickname Little Cassiopeia.

constellations.name: Leo
constellations.story: To the ancient Greeks it was the Nemean lion, killed by the hero Heracles as one of his twelve labours.

constellations.name: Leo Minor
constellations.story: Johannes Hevelius created the smaller lion in 1687; its only star with a Greek letter is Beta, and it has no Alpha.

constellations.name: Lepus
constellations.story: The hare crouches just south of Orion and is sometimes shown being chased by the hunter or his dogs.

constellations.name: Libra
constellations.story: Babylonians knew it as the scales or as the Claws of the Scorpion; its star names still mean the northern and southern claw.

constellations.name: Lupus
constellations.story: In ancient times an unnamed wild animal held by Centaurus, until Hipparchus made it a separate constellation, the beast, in the 2nd century BC.

constellations.name: Lynx
constellations.story: Hevelius introduced it in the late 17th century, naming it for its faintness and declaring that only the lynx-eyed would be able to see it.

constellations.name: Lyra
constellations.story: In Greek myth it represents the lyre of Orpheus; its brightest star, Vega, is a corner of the Summer Triangle.

constellations.name: Mensa
constellations.story: Lacaille named it after Table Mountain near his observatory at Cape Town; it is the faintest constellation recognised by the IAU.

constellations.name: Microscopium
constellations.story: One of Lacaille's 18th-century constellations depicting scientific instruments; even its brightest star, Gamma Microscopii, is only magnitude 4.7.

constellations.name: Monoceros
constellations.story: The unicorn first appeared for certain on a globe by Petrus Plancius in 1612 or 1613; it lies on the celestial equator beside Orion.

constellations.name: Musca
constellations.story: The only official constellation depicting an insect; Bayer called it Apis, the bee, a name it kept for the next two centuries.

constellations.name: Norma
constellations.story: Lacaille named it in the 18th century after the carpenter's square; the Norma Arm of the Milky Way passes through it.

constellations.name: Octans
constellations.story: Lacaille devised it in 1752 after the octant, a navigational instrument; the south celestial pole lies within its borders.

constellations.name: Ophiuchus
constellations.story: A man grasping a snake, identified in Roman-era myth with the healer Asclepius; the snake he holds is the constellation Serpens.

constellations.name: Orion
constellations.story: Named after a hunter of Greek myth, it holds Rigel, Betelgeuse and the three stars of Orion's Belt.

constellations.name: Pavo
constellations.story: One of the Southern Birds, probably conceived by Plancius from Dutch navigators' observations; its brightest star, Alpha Pavonis, is named Peacock.

constellations.name: Pegasus
constellations.story: Named after the winged horse of Greek myth; its star 51 Pegasi was the first Sun-like star found to have a planet.

constellations.name: Perseus
constellations.story: Named after the Greek hero who beheaded Medusa; its star Algol, the Demon's Head, represents the Gorgon's head.

constellations.name: Phoenix
constellations.story: The mythical phoenix, first shown in Bayer's atlas of 1603; its brightest star, Ankaa, takes its name from the Arabic for the phoenix.

constellations.name: Pictor
constellations.story: Lacaille's painter's easel; its second-brightest star, Beta Pictoris, is surrounded by an unusual dust disc and has planets of its own.

constellations.name: Pisces
constellations.story: In Greek myth the two fishes are linked with Aphrodite and Eros, who became fishes to escape the monster Typhon.

constellations.name: Piscis Austrinus
constellations.story: The southern fish of Ptolemy's list; Fomalhaut, traditionally its mouth, is the only star in it brighter than fourth magnitude.

constellations.name: Puppis
constellations.story: The stern of the ship Argo Navis, sailed by Jason and the Argonauts; it is the largest of the ship's three parts.

constellations.name: Pyxis
constellations.story: Lacaille introduced the mariner's compass in the 18th century, placing it beside the stars of the old ship Argo Navis.

constellations.name: Reticulum
constellations.story: Lacaille named it after the reticle in his telescope eyepiece, a net of crosshairs used to measure star positions.

constellations.name: Sagitta
constellations.story: Eratosthenes called it the arrow with which Apollo killed the Cyclopes; it is the third-smallest constellation.

constellations.name: Sagittarius
constellations.story: Usually drawn as a centaur drawing a bow; the centre of the Milky Way lies in its westernmost part.

constellations.name: Scorpius
constellations.story: In one Greek myth it is the giant scorpion sent to kill the boastful hunter Orion, both then raised to the sky by Zeus.

constellations.name: Sculptor
constellations.story: Lacaille introduced it in the 18th century as Apparatus Sculptoris, the sculptor's studio; the name was later shortened.

constellations.name: Scutum
constellations.story: Hevelius named it in 1684 for the shield of King John III Sobieski, celebrating his victory at the Battle of Vienna.

constellations.name: Serpens
constellations.story: The only constellation split into two separate parts, the head and the tail of the snake, either side of Ophiuchus.

constellations.name: Sextans
constellations.story: Hevelius introduced it in 1687 after the astronomical sextant, an instrument he used often in his observations.

constellations.name: Taurus
constellations.story: In Greek myth Zeus took the form of a white bull to carry off Europa; it holds the Pleiades and the Hyades.

constellations.name: Telescopium
constellations.story: One of Lacaille's 18th-century constellations depicting scientific instruments; it was later much reduced in size by Baily and Gould.

constellations.name: Triangulum
constellations.story: Its three brightest stars form a long, narrow triangle; it also holds the Triangulum Galaxy, a member of our Local Group.

constellations.name: Triangulum Australe
constellations.story: First shown by Plancius in 1589 as Triangulus Antarcticus; its three main stars outshine those of the northern Triangulum.

constellations.name: Tucana
constellations.story: One of the Southern Birds created by Plancius, the toucan contains most of the Small Magellanic Cloud and the cluster 47 Tucanae.

constellations.name: Ursa Major
constellations.story: Its seven main stars form the Big Dipper or Plough; in Greek myth the bear is the nymph Callisto, transformed by Hera.

constellations.name: Ursa Minor
constellations.story: The Little Bear, or Little Dipper, has long guided navigators, because it contains Polaris, the north pole star.

constellations.name: Vela
constellations.story: The sails of the old ship Argo Navis; two of its stars help form the False Cross, sometimes mistaken for the Southern Cross.

constellations.name: Virgo
constellations.story: The maiden is the second-largest constellation, after Hydra, and the largest of the zodiac; its brightest star is Spica.

constellations.name: Volans
constellations.story: The flying fish, shortened from Piscis Volans, was one of twelve constellations Plancius created from Dutch navigators' observations.

constellations.name: Vulpecula
constellations.story: Hevelius created it in the late 17th century as a little fox with a goose in its jaws; it lies within the Summer Triangle.
